# Generator shortcut answer

The strongest plausible canonical-fitting shortcut is **`marker_must_be_key`**:

> Infer the first row-major nonzero/non-8 body colour as the marker, but recolour it by quadrant only when that marker colour also appears in the 2×2 key; otherwise return the grid unchanged.

This is strong because it fits all six usable canonical input/output pairs recorded by the final census. In the canonical data, the body marker happens to be one of the four key colours, so the extra condition is never exposed.

## How I checked it

I validated the generated input with `self_check` (no errors), then ran the supported public command:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 0a9e3d364bb3 \
  --input ../checks/shortcut-witness-input.json \
  --out ../checks/shortcut-witness-apply-replay.json
```

The replayed receipt is `checks/shortcut-witness-apply-replay.json` (the original equivalent receipt is also retained as `checks/shortcut-witness-apply.json`). It records selected generator SHA-256 `42cf51fb28002b7a663a6816387b5050047798392f5f79827a7204336511ed42`, executed/catalog rule hash `debd91c13f07`, a valid Racket output, and matching input/output hashes. The independent Python mirror matched that Racket output exactly; all combined facts are in `checks/shortcut-witness.json`.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

**Yes.** `marker_not_in_key` is one of the unchanged four production profiles, and the exact witness above was emitted by the final source. More importantly, the final seven-demo-plus-one-query policy spans two complete profile cycles. Therefore every possible one-pair query rotation leaves at least one marker-outside-key demonstration, so this shortcut cannot survive the demonstrations merely because its sole witness became the query. The 300-lesson census found 0/2,400 ambiguous rotations, and the cyclic-start probe found 0/1,536 failures against the declared rivals.
